title: Test two machine light curtains with their test rods and tag out the one that fails
instruction: Test each machine's light curtain with its test rod at the bottom, middle and top of its field, and put the DO NOT USE tag in the holder of any machine whose curtain fails.
context: Operators and maintenance workers prove a machine's safety light curtain before the shift by pushing the supplied test rod (30 mm for a hand-protection curtain) through its field at the bottom, middle and top while watching the receiver's lamp: it must go red every time. A curtain that does not trip is taken out of service with a tag on the machine. Done by general maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5 million US workers), industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041, about 400,000) and packaging and filling machine operators (51-9111, about 370,000); a daily or per-shift check under IEC 61496-2 and the machine's own safety instructions. Here two benchtop machines stand side by side, one curtain has a dead beam and the other is sound; which one changes every trial.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Two identical safety light curtains, each a pair of 40 x 40 mm yellow housings 230 mm tall on 90 x 90 mm foot plates, protected height 150 mm (52 to 202 mm above the table), 400 mm between the lenses; field centres at (0.44, 0.38) and (0.44, -0.38), the field plane facing the robot (x = 0.44). Each has 8 beams 20 mm apart with 10 mm lenses (30 mm resolution) and a lamp on the receiver's top cap: green while clear, red while a beam is interrupted. Each machine has a 30 mm test rod (300 mm, 110 g, aluminium tube with yellow and black bands) resting on two saddles in front of its field, tip 5 cm short of the plane, and an empty tag holder (a slot 8 mm wide, 90 mm long) 15 cm in front of the plane beside the field. A red 76 x 127 x 5 mm DO NOT USE tag stands in a rack at (0.26, 0). One receiver has a dead beam channel (the one 117 mm above the table); which machine it is is drawn at random every trial. The dead beam is seen only through the lamp: the rod trips the faulty lamp at the bottom and top but not where it covers only the dead beam (axis 107 to 127 mm).
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video. (1) Left field tested: a rod has been pushed through it, axis within 15 degrees of the field's normal, tip at least 4 cm past the plane, between the posts, three times: bottom (axis 52-102 mm), middle (axis 108-126 mm, where the rod covers the dead beam alone; the rest of 102-152 mm does not count) and top (152-202 mm). (2) The same for the right field. (3) The tag stands in the holder of the machine whose curtain missed the rod (lower edge in the slot within 12 mm along it and 4 mm across, upright within 6 degrees), after that curtain's three passes, the exposing middle one included, and none in the other holder. (4) With steps 1 to 3: both rods out of both fields and every gripper at least 3 cm from the tag and the rods. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four steps have held together, without a break, for 1 s with the rods and the tag within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where they were when that second began; step points stop at 0.8. 0 overall if a rod or the tag is off the table.
reset_notes: Put each rod on its saddles and the tag in the rack; stand the tag holders empty. A coin flip chooses which of the two bench test fixtures has channel 4 (117 mm up) open: take its two-pin link out on that receiver board and fit all eight links on the other. Check each by hand with the rod: the sound lamp stays red all the way up, the faulty one goes green near 117 mm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; curtains, holders, saddles and rack are fixtures. The trip lamp is a declared code effect: a red and a green disc swapped on the receiver's cap, red while a rod covers the whole 10 mm lens of a working beam. The faulty machine (drawn at random each episode) has one beam that never trips; the real trial uses a bench fixture with that channel's link removed. Tag is a 5 mm rigid sign in a slot. Rod 110 g (typical).
scores: Dream-1 run (1,200 steps, left machine faulty): 0.0 (both arms hovered near the rods, no rod pass, tag not moved); demo: 1.0 at step 798-799 in every run, with the left machine faulty and with the right one faulty
